## Outline

- Understand the principles of image classification in UAS mapping  
- Differentiate between **supervised**, **unsupervised** learning methods
- Derive spectral indices from RGB and multispectral UAS imagery and read them as features
- Learn how to apply classification workflows in **GRASS**  
- Interpret and validate classification results using **accuracy assessment metrics**  
- Explore real-world applications of UAS classification for **environmental monitoring**

## Supplemental materials

- [Rapid-DEM: Rapid Topographic Updates through Satellite Change Detection and UAS Data Fusion](https://www.mdpi.com/2072-4292/14/7/1718)
- Jensen, J.R. Introductory Digital Image Processing: A Remote Sensing Perspective, 4th ed.; Prentice Hall Press: Upper Saddle River, NJ, USA, 2015.
- [i.vi](https://grass.osgeo.org/grass85/manuals/i.vi.html) manual page: the vegetation indices GRASS computes and their formulas
- [UAS for Wetland Mapping and Hydrological Modeling](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs11171997), Jeziorska, Remote Sensing 11(17), 2019: a review of UAS sensors, including the multispectral cameras compared in the lecture
- [Absolute Radiometric Calibration Evaluation of UAS Headwall and MicaSense Sensors](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs17223738), Shrestha et al., Remote Sensing 17(22), 2025: the USGS calibration campaign whose data the lab uses
- [Guidelines for calibration of uncrewed aircraft systems imagery](https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/ofr20231033/full), Sampath et al., USGS Open-File Report 2023-1033
